question: A 3-month-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his mom for breathing difficulty after a recent fall. His parents say that he rolled off of the mattress and landed on the hard wood floor earlier today. After an extensive physical exam, he is found to have many purplish bruises and retinal hemorrhages. A non-contrast head CT scan shows a subdural hemorrhage. He was treated in the hospital with full recovery from his symptoms. Which of the following is the most important follow up plan?

options.ope: Referral to genetics for further testing

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "3-month-old boy" -> "breathing difficulty after a fall" -> "purplish bruises and retinal hemorrhages" -> "subdural hemorrhage on head CT scan" -> "treated in hospital with full recovery" -> "possible child abuse" -> "inform child protective services" -> 80%

CHAIN: "3-month-old boy" -> "fall from mattress to hard wood floor" -> "purplish bruises and retinal hemorrhages" -> "subdural hemorrhage on head CT scan" -> "possible non-accidental trauma" -> "inform child protective services" -> 75%
enhanced_information: Given the presentation of a 3-month-old boy with purplish bruises, retinal hemorrhages, and a subdural hemorrhage following a fall, there is a high suspicion of possible non-accidental trauma. The most important follow-up plan would be to inform child protective services to investigate further and ensure the child's safety.
analysis: The presentation of a 3-month-old boy with multiple bruises, retinal hemorrhages, and a subdural hemorrhage after a fall raises concerns for non-accidental trauma (NAT) or child abuse. Given the suspicious findings, the most important follow-up plan would be to inform child protective services to ensure the safety and well-being of the child.
